extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs), plant compliance officers, environmental managers, and regulators implementing/complying with EPA Subpart TTTT/TTTTa GHG standards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for demonstrating compliance with EPA CO2 emission standards for affected steam generating units, IGCCs, and stationary combustion turbines (Subpart TTTT and TTTTa), including monitoring, calculation, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output-based energy calculation (§60.5520 / §60.5535(a)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an output-based standard, calculate the total gross or net energy output for the affected EGU's compliance period by summing the hourly gross or net energy output values for all valid operating hours determined under paragraph (a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must follow §60.5520 procedures; sum hourly gross or net output values for all valid operating hours in the applicable compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat-input total calculation (§60.5535(a)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to a heat input-based standard, calculate the total heat input for each fuel fired during the compliance period including all valid operating hours and consistent with any fuel-specific procedures in your selected monitoring option under §60.5535(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate total heat input separately for each fuel using all valid operating hours; follow fuel-specific monitoring option procedures when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 mass emissions rate calculation — output-based
rubrics_metrics.description: For output-based standards, calculate CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/MWh) by dividing the total CO2 mass emissions (per §60.5535(a)(4)) by the total gross or net energy output (per §60.5535(a)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round result: two significant figures if <1,000; three significant figures if ≥1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 mass emissions rate calculation — heat-input based
rubrics_metrics.description: For heat input-based standards, calculate CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) by dividing the total CO2 mass emissions (per §60.5535(a)(4)) by the total heat input (per §60.5535(a)(6)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round off the result to two significant figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance demonstration timing and standard comparison (§60.5520(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month compliance period, the CO2 mass emissions rate must be determined according to specified procedures and must be less than or equal to the applicable CO2 emissions standard in table 1 or 2 to this subpart, or the standard calculated per §60.5525(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine CO2 mass emissions rate per paragraphs (a)(1) through (8) for each 12-operating-month period and compare to applicable table/section standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report percentage of valid operating hours (§60.5555(a)(2)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period: (total number of valid operating hours in the period divided by total operating hours in that period) × 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid operating hours defined in §60.5540(a)(1); include this percentage in required reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report applicable CO2 emissions standard identification (§60.5555(a)(2)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §60.5520, report the CO2 emissions standard (as identified in table 1 or 2 to this subpart) with which the affected EGU must comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include table/section identification of the applicable standard in reporting submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for captured CO2 (§60.5555(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the applicable standard, report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either: (1) report under 40 CFR part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer captured CO2 to an EGU/facility that reports under RR or VV if injection occurs off-site; or (3) transfer to a facility with an innovative technology waiver per paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow subpart PP reporting plus the specified on-site/off-site/waiver reporting pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process for captured CO2 transfer (§60.5555(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request a waiver from the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV. Applicant must demonstrate technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and not cause unreasonable risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator considers operating history, whether technology increases emissions of pollutants other than CO2, permanence of storage; Administrator may test or require tests, grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, withdraw approval on evidence of releases, and will provide public notice of applications and proposed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of electric sales for combustion turbines (§60.5560(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Stationary combustion turbines must keep records of electric sales to determine the applicable subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain electric sales records sufficient to demonstrate subcategory applicability (gross vs net energy output or heat-input based eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to demonstrate system emergency operation (§60.5560(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: To demonstrate the facility operated during a system emergency, keep: (1) documentation that the system emergency was in effect and duration from the issuing entity; (2) documentation that the emergency included the affected source/region; and (3) documentation that facility was instructed to increase output beyond planned dispatch or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch by a Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or ISO/RTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records are required to exclude emissions/output during system emergencies for applicability and compliance per §60.5525a(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Annual capacity factor (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual capacity factor = ratio between actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and potential heat input if operated 8,760 hours/year at base load rating. Excludes actual/potential heat input from non-combustion sources (e.g., solar thermal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only combustion-derived heat input when computing annual capacity factor for applicability/exemption determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Base load rating (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Base load rating = maximum amount of heat input that an EGU can combust on a steady state basis plus maximum heat input from non-combustion sources, as determined by physical design/characteristics at ISO conditions; for stationary combustion turbines includes heat input from duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base load rating used in determining applicability, subcategory thresholds, and emission standard selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Coal (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal includes all solid fuels classified as anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, or lignite by ASTM D388-99R04, coal refuse, petroleum coke, and synthetic fuels derived from coal used for creating useful heat (e.g., solvent-refined coal, gasified coal not meeting natural gas definition, coal-oil or coal-water mixtures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition applies for purposes of the subpart; incorporated ASTM references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Combined cycle unit (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined cycle unit = a stationary combustion turbine whose exhaust heat is recovered by a heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG) to generate additional electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify affected unit types and applicable monitoring/test methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Combined heat and power (CHP) unit (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: CHP (cogeneration) = an electric generating unit that simultaneously produces electric (or mechanical) and useful thermal output from the same primary energy source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules (e.g., net-electric sales calculation) apply to CHP units in several provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Design efficiency and approved methods (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design efficiency = rated overall net efficiency (electric plus useful thermal output) on a lower heating value basis at the base load rating, ISO conditions, and maximum useful thermal output. Determined using ASME PTC 22-2014, ASME PTC 46-1996, ISO 2314:2009(E), or an Administrator-approved alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design efficiency measurement method must be one of the listed standards or an Administrator-approved alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Distillate oil (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distillate oil = fuel oils meeting ASTM D396-98 (fuel oil #1 and #2), diesel fuel oils as defined in ASTM D975-08a, kerosene per ASTM D3699-08, biodiesel per ASTM D6751-11b, or biodiesel blends per ASTM D7467-10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASTM references incorporated by reference; use these specifications when identifying fuel types for monitoring/standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — ISO conditions (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: ISO conditions = 288 Kelvin (15 °C), 60% relative humidity, and 101.3 kilopascals pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for determining base load rating and design efficiency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Net-electric sales (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: Net-electric sales = (1) gross electric sales to the utility distribution system minus purchased power; or (2) for CHP facilities meeting certain thresholds, gross electric sales minus purchased power of the thermal host facility(ies). Electricity supplied to facilities producing electricity to offset auxiliary loads is included; electric sales during a system emergency are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net-electric sales calculations affect subcategory assignment (gross vs net output-based standards) and applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — System emergency (§60.5580)
rubrics_metrics.description: System emergency = periods when the Reliability Coordinator has declared an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2 or its successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System emergency definition triggers exclusions and alternate compliance treatments when properly documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — CO2 emission standards for steam generating units and IGCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric CO2 emission standards by affected EGU category: Newly constructed steam generating unit or IGCC: 640 kg CO2/MWh gross (1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross). Reconstructed units and modified units have specified values and unit-specific limits (floors) depending on base load rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical values ≥1,000 have minimum 3 significant figures; values <1,000 have minimum 2 significant figures. Modified-unit limits based on best historical annual CO2 emission rate (2002 to modification date) but not lower than specified floors (820 or 910 kg CO2/MWh depending on base load rating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 — CO2 emission standards for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: CO2 emission standards for stationary combustion turbines vary by operating profile and fuel composition: e.g., newly constructed/reconstructed turbines that supply more than design efficiency or 50% of potential output and combust >90% natural gas: 450 kg CO2/MWh gross (1,000 lb CO2/MWh) or 470 kg CO2/MWh net (1,030 lb CO2/MWh). Other rows specify 50 kg CO2/GJ heat input for certain configurations and 50–69 kg CO2/GJ for turbines combusting ≤90% natural gas as determined per §60.5525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards may be gross- or net-energy-output based as approved by the Administrator; see table and §60.5520 for which term applies to a given owner/operator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Subpart A general provisions (Table 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which general provisions of Part 60 (Subpart A) apply to Subpart TTTT, with explanations and exceptions (e.g., monitoring done under part 75; performance test provisions may not apply; certain notifications and recordkeeping limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review table for specific §60.x applicability and noted exceptions (e.g., §60.8(a) Performance tests: No; §60.13 monitoring requirements: No (monitoring under part 75) except §60.13(i): Yes where Administrator can approve alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart TTTTa applicability thresholds (construction/reconstruction/ modification after May 23, 2023)
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG standards in Subpart TTTTa apply to steam generating units/IGCCs that combust coal and commence modification after May 23, 2023, and to stationary combustion turbines that commence construction or reconstruction after May 23, 2023, provided the EGU has base load rating >260 GJ/h and serves generator(s) capable of selling >25 MW to the utility distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §60.5509a for the specific numeric thresholds and date triggers for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart TTTTa exemptions (§60.5509a(b)(1)-(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight categories of exclusions from Subpart TTTTa, including units with net-electric sales never exceeding one-third of potential output and subject to enforceable permit limiting sales, EGUs deriving ≥50% heat input from non-fossil fuels and limited to ≤10% annual capacity factor by permit, CHP units with enforceable limits, certain small effective generation capacities (≤25 MW), municipal waste combustors and certain waste incinerators subject to other subparts, modifications with ≤10% hourly CO2 emissions increase, and EGUs deriving >50% heat input from an industrial process that yields no external output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exemption has detailed conditions (e.g., federally enforceable permit limits, numeric thresholds) that must be met to qualify for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollutants regulated and cross-reference to PSD/Title V definitions (§60.5515a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subpart regulates greenhouse gases in the form of a limitation on carbon dioxide emissions. For purposes of PSD and Title V thresholds, the pollutant 'subject to the standard promulgated under section 111' shall be treated as the pollutant otherwise 'subject to regulation' per certain 40 CFR 51.166/52.21/70.2/71.2 definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mapping affects how GHG thresholds are interpreted in PSD/Title V contexts; review cited CFR provisions for cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to meet applicable gross/net energy output standard and permit content (§60.5520a(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must not discharge CO2 in excess of the applicable gross or net energy output standard in table 1; operating permits must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methodologies based on the applicable gross or net energy output standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where paragraphs (c) or (d) apply, the term 'gross or net energy output' to be used is specified for each source; permit conditions must align with the chosen output basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition option to comply with net energy output standard (§60.5520a(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/operator of a stationary combustion turbine may petition the Administrator to comply with the alternate net energy output standard; if granted, the turbine must comply with the net standard and have permit monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting based on net energy output; owners/operators may petition to switch back to gross standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be in writing; effective date begins when Administrator grants the petition; permit must reflect monitoring based on the granted basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fuel exemption and monitoring tiers (§60.5520a(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines permitted to burn only uniform fuels (consistent chemical composition leading to consistent emission rate ≤69 kg/GJ) are not subject to monitoring or reporting requirements under this subpart other than maintaining purchase records. Owners/operators permitted to burn non-uniform fuels or fuels with emission rate >69 kg/GJ must follow monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting required to complete heat input-based calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists examples of uniform fuels (hydrogen, natural gas, methane, butane, ethane, propane, naphtha, jet fuel, kerosene, No.1/No.2 fuel oil, biodiesel). If relying on exemption, keep purchase records for permitted fuels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance averaging and monthly determination (§60.5525a(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the CO2 emission standards shall be determined on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis; owners/operators must determine compliance monthly by calculating the average CO2 emissions rate at the end of the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combustion turbines that qualify for the uniform fuel exemption are only required to maintain purchase records; others must follow the rolling-average monthly determination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input-based standard calculation method (Equation 1) (§60.5525a(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For input-based CO2 standards, total heat input from natural gas (HTIPng) and from other fuels (HTIPo) must be determined and used in Equation 1 to compute the applicable emissions standard during the compliance period using fixed allowable emission rates (50 kg/GJ for natural gas; 69 kg/GJ for other fuels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equation parameters and units (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) are specified; owners/operators must use one of monitoring methods under §60.5535a(d)(2) to determine HTIP values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific emissions rate election for certain turbines (§60.5525a(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of base load combustion turbines with base load rating <2,110 GJ/h and/or certain turbines burning fuels other than natural gas may elect to determine a site-specific emissions rate using the provided equations for base load and intermediate load turbines (Equations 2 and 3). HIER_A (heat input-based emissions rate of actual fuel) must not exceed 69 kg/GJ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equations include parameters such as BLER_L, BLER_S, BLR_L, BLR_S, BLR_A, HIER_A, and HIER_NG; follow definitions and numeric BLER/ILER values given in the text when applying equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation and maintenance standard (§60.5525a(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times, operate and maintain each affected EGU, including associated equipment and monitors, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice. The Administrator will determine consistency using available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may use fuel use records, monitoring results, review of O&M procedures/records, required reports, and inspections to determine compliance with O&M expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance determination timing and first operating month rules (§60.5525a(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the end of the initial 12-operating-month compliance period, make an initial compliance determination. The first operating month of the initial period depends on whether the EGU commenced commercial operation or is a modified/reconstructed unit and on when emissions reporting is required to begin under §60.5555a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subclauses (c)(1)-(3) define how to determine the first operating month for newly operating EGUs and modified/reconstructed units; follow those rules when initiating the first 12-operating-month compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: System emergency exclusions and standards during emergency (§60.5525a(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions and output generated during a system emergency (per §60.5580a) are excluded from applicability and compliance if sufficient documentation per §60.5560a(i) is provided. Relevant standard during a system emergency: (i) intermediate and base load combustion turbines comply with low load combustion turbine standard in table 1; (ii) modified steam generating units must meet 230 lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the documentation listed in §60.5560a(i) to qualify for exclusions; the applicable standard during emergencies depends on subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan preparation and submission (§60.5535a(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a monitoring plan to quantify hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h). The electronic portion of the monitoring plan must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool prior to reporting emissions data or monitoring system certification results. Plans must be maintained and updated as necessary and submitted by the Designated Representative (DR) or delegated agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plan must be in place prior to reporting; DR/Alternate DR or delegated agent is responsible for submittal; follow ECMPS Client Tool procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS and alternatives for CO2 concentration and flow monitoring (§60.5535a(b)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-burning EGUs, you must install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) and a flow monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i). For other EGUs, CEMS is optional. As an alternative to direct CO2 measurement (provided no carbon separation is used), a certified O2 monitor may be used to calculate hourly average CO2 concentrations per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(iii). If CO2 measured on a dry basis, a continuous moisture monitor per 40 CFR 75.11(b) is required or use an appropriate fuel-specific default moisture value or petition under 40 CFR 75.66 for a site-specific default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using CEMS or O2-derived CO2, meet certification and QA procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B. Coal-fired units required to use CEMS; others may opt to use emissions calculation methods in paragraph (c) if exclusively combusting liquid/gaseous fuels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and quality assurance for continuous monitoring systems (§60.5535a(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions must meet applicable certification and QA procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the certification, QA, and QA/QC procedures exactly as specified in Part 75 to ensure valid monitoring data for compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates (§60.5535a(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions; do not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to exhaust gas flow rate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow data used in CO2 calculations must be the unadjusted measured volumetric flow rates; prohibited from applying specific Part 75 bias adjustments to flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow monitor reference method selection and RATA setup; pitot tube calibration (§60.5535a(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an appropriate reference method to set up (characterize) the flow monitor and perform on-going Relative Accuracy Test Audits (RATAs) per 40 CFR part 75. If using a Type-S pitot tube or pitot tube assembly for flow RATAs, you must calibrate it and may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot tube coefficient specified in Method 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and document an appropriate reference method under Part 75 for flow monitor characterization and RATA procedures; perform pitot tube calibration rather than relying on default coefficient when using Type-S pitot tubes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions calculation steps and record/report requirements (§60.5535a(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) only for 'valid operating hours' as defined in §60.5540(a)(1): (i) obtain hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) from Equation F-11 in appendix F to Part 75 (wet basis) or appendix F section 4.2 (dry basis); (ii) multiply each hourly CO2 mass emission rate by EGU/stack operating time to convert to tons; (iii) multiply tons by 907.2 to convert to kg and round to nearest kg; (iv) hourly tons/h values and operating times must be recorded under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and reported under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6) and used to calculate hourly CO2 mass emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform calculations only for valid operating hours; follow specified equations for wet/dry basis; round to nearest kg and retain/submit the underlying hourly data as required by Part 75 electronic reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative hourly CO2 determination for liquid/gaseous fuel-only EGUs (§60.5535a(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the affected EGU exclusively combusts liquid and/or gaseous fuel, as an alternative to the CEMS-based approach in paragraph (b), the owner/operator may determine hourly CO2 mass emissions according to the alternative procedures in paragraph (c)(1)–(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (c) provides alternative calculation/monitoring pathways for liquid/gaseous-fuel-only units; consult paragraph (c) for the detailed alternative methods (not fully included in this chunk).
